thread:
alex: Heads-up — we just received a DSAR (user@example.com) asking for deletion of their personal data including generated embeddings and associated request logs. They specifically asked to confirm deletion and audit evidence. Need input on RBAC, KMS access, and whether we should apply for a temporary retention exception for backup snapshots.
maya: Do we have proof-of-request and identity? legal will need that before we proceed. Also scope: embeddings + raw logs + analytics traces?
lena-legal: Please confirm what exact artifacts they want removed. We need requester verification steps (email confirm + recent activity). If it's a verified subject request, we can proceed; otherwise we should ask for more info.
alex: Verified already — they sent the signed request and ID. They listed: all embeddings derived from their account, request logs, and any cached inference artifacts in the private deployment.
owen: OK. Technical thoughts: embeddings live in vectorstore V1 (encrypted with customer-KMS-key alias/redwood-prod-vec). Deleting requires KMS decrypt to locate shards then remove vectors and update index. If key policy is restrictive we need admin-kms role. Also backups: nightly snapshots are on S3 with server-side encryption; lifecycle retention might keep copies for 30d.
sara: Audit concerns: we'll need a verifiable deletion record (who deleted, when, what keys/ids). Our audit-logs pipeline currently records S3 object deletions and DB row deletes, but not necessarily high-level DSAR IDs. We should attach a DSAR id to the deletion transaction and emit an audit event.
alex: Agreed. Can we patch the audit-log to include dsar_id for manual deletes? Short-term patch ok, long-term hook in the delete service. Also asking: do we require a retention-exception for backups, or can we trigger expunge from backups immediately?
owen: We cannot retroactively delete from immutable Glacier-style archives without retention exception and legal approval. For regular S3 with versioning, we can schedule an expedited lifecycle or use admin delete with retention-exception header (requires documented approval).
maya: ops question — who has the RBAC to perform admin delete on the vectorstore and S3? I assume infra-admin + security-admin. Need a temporary grant path (just-in-time) and audit trail.
sara: Proposed JIT flow: create a short-lived role 'dsar-deleter' with MFA, scoped to this request, TTL 2 hours, log every action to audit-collector with dsar_id tag. Approvals: security + legal sign-off in thread.
lena-legal: Legal OK with JIT approach provided we keep chain-of-custody logs and requester proof. Please include retention-exception ticket if backups are immutable.
irina-bot: automation: Created ticket REQ-2024-1789 in retention-exceptions queue. Added checklist template: verify_requester -> snapshot_scope -> create_jit_role -> run_delete -> audit_proof.
owen: Deletion steps (draft):
```
# 1. tag dsar_id on vectorstore rows
# 2. assume dsar-deleter role
# 3. delete vectors by id batch
# 4. trash S3 objects and update object manifest
# 5. trigger audit event: {"dsar_id": "REQ-2024-1789", "deleted_ids": [...], "actor": "owen"}
```
maya: One technical risk: ongoing inference may have items in KV cache / in-flight requests referencing deleted embeddings. We should place the customer's account into a hold (deny inference) for a short window before deletion to avoid race conditions.
sara: Add step: disable account tokens + purge caches + wait 1 minute milestone, then delete. Document exact timestamps in audit.
alex: Who wants to own running the delete? I can take coordination + comms with customer, Owen + Maya to run infra steps, Sara to own audit, Lena to confirm. Need sign-off in thread to proceed.
lena-legal: Signed: Lena (legal) — verified request, approve JIT role and deletion for REQ-2024-1789. Keep evidence packet.
omment: (typo correction): owen: ack — I'll prepare the IAM policy and a one-time key access list. Will post policy snippet here once ready.
owen: IAM snippet draft:
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:DeleteObject","s3:DeleteObjectVersion"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-vectors/*"]},
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey"],"Resource":["arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/*"]}
  ]
}
```
maya: Looks fine, add condition for aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent and aws:RequestTag/dsar_id requirement.
oven: Will do. ETA 30m for role & brief runbook.
irina-bot: audit: scheduled evidence export to legal bucket (s3://redwood-legal-evidence/REQ-2024-1789/) after deletion.
sara: After we execute, I'll compose the deletion certificate (hash of deleted ids + timestamps + operator sig) and attach to the evidence bucket.
alex: Great. One more risk: vuln triage — discovered a race where rollback of deletion could leak references back into the vector index if partial failure occurs. Owen, add a post-mortem step to the runbook and a rollback plan (rebuild index from before-state snapshot).
owen: Noted. I'll add transaction logs and an atomic manifest update to avoid half-applies.
maya: OK proceeding on hold. I'll create the short-lived role once Owen posts final policy.
alex: Thanks everyone. I'll update customer with expected timeline (3-4 hours). Will post final confirmation and attach audit certificate when done. :thumbsup:
